answers.ask: Is this one small stretch of beach with a few chairs, or a longer shoreline players can walk along between words?
answers.answer: Make it one small stretch of beach with a few beach chairs and a sea outlook, so players stay focused on the spelling game.

answers.ask: Is everyone spelling the same word at once and racing, or does each player get their own?
answers.answer: Everyone should hear and spell the same word at once, with points awarded for correct answers.

scene_prompt: Create a realistic third-person 3D beach setting: one small stretch of shoreline with a clear sea outlook, sandy ground, and a few beach chairs arranged facing the water. Keep the area compact and focused around the seated beach-chair viewing area.
agent_notes: Puzzle's Word / Quiz Puzzle preset is written for exactly this prompt — spelling the word that shows up on the screen — and its genre note warns that these get filed under Party & Casual instead, so I led with Puzzle; Party & Casual is named second because its own boundary note has a real claim here (nothing is spatially gated, the layout job is hosting the question and the crowd) and because everyone answers the same word simultaneously for points. Naming it second costs nothing and is what lets the beach chairs land on its social-hub gathering row and the points on trigger-scoring, neither of which Puzzle can express. I kept the preset's puzzle-open shape, which is right for one small unenclosed stretch of beach, and its facade-clue as the display facing the chairs where the word appears, but dropped gate-solve because no forward progress is blocked by solving anything; the sea outlook is water-body as a backdrop rather than swimmable volume, so its CHECK clears. SET is the call I made without a user: the activity is typing while seated on a flat beach, so nothing has to be traversed or jumped to, and SET skips those checks without skipping any of the build.
